newsitem.title: UK: Littlewoods sees healthy interest in shops.
newsitem.headline: Littlewoods sees healthy interest in shops.

text.p: British retail-to-football pools company Littlewoods has received "healthy interest" for the 135 shops it put up for sale last month, a spokeswoman said.
She said the company still wanted to sell the stores to a single buyer, which could be a consortium of several companies, rather than spinning off individual stores.
Newspaper reports on Monday suggested that chemist and stores chain Boots Plc was planning to approach other retailers to see if they might be interested in combining in a bid.
Littlewoods had set a deadline of April 11 for preliminary bids, according to the Evening Standard newspaper.
Boots declined to comment on the reports.
The 135 Littlewoods stores up for sale include several sites which could prove attractive locations for large Boots outlets.

Britain's largest supermarket chain Tesco Plc last week said it had requested information on the stores from Littlewoods but that it was unlikely to buy them as it had a lot on after its purchase of Irish supermarkets from Associated British Foods (ABF).
Littlewoods said in March that it was looking into the possibility of selling its stores division, estimated to be worth over 500 million stg.
